description.para: Strongly-typed wrappers for converting dynamic values and expressions to specific types recognised by µTest++ comparators.

These type aliases provide a type-safe mechanism for explicitly converting values to the required types for µTest++ test expressions and comparators. Each alias is a wrapper around detail::value<T>, ensuring that the value is treated as the specified type within the framework.
The to_* forms replaced the older _i, _u8, etc. aliases, which were deprecated in version 3.2.0.

description.para: The v5.0.1 names of the to_* type wrappers.

The Boost UT style names, with a leading underscore, kept for compatibility with the existing applications. Each one is an alias of the corresponding to_* wrapper, so the wrapped values are compared and reported in the same way. They do not conflict with the literal operators with the same suffixes (42_i), which are in the literals namespace.
GCC reports the deprecation only when the alias names the type of a declaration, not when it is used in an expression, as in _i (expr); Clang reports it in both cases.

parameterdescription.para: The type of the wrapped value.

xrefdescription.para: pass plain values to eq() and the other comparators (since 5.1.0)

briefdescription.para: Wraps a floating-point value with an explicit comparison tolerance.

detaileddescription.para: The floating-point literals (1.5_d) and wrappers (to_d{ 1.5 }) compare with a tolerance derived from the number of decimals written (0.1 for 1.5). approx() makes the tolerance explicit, independent of how the value is written. All six comparisons apply it: values whose difference is less than the tolerance are equal, and neither less nor greater. If both operands have a tolerance, the smaller one is used.
For a single comparison, also of integers, the approx (lhs, rhs, epsilon) function comparator may be used instead.

parameterdescription.para: The floating-point type of the value.
The expected value.
The tolerance, converted to T.

simplesect.para: A detail::value<T> wrapper, recognised by the comparators and the operators.

simplesect.title: Deprecated
simplesect.para: Use the function comparator approx (lhs, rhs, epsilon) instead (since 5.1.0).

xrefdescription.para: use approx (lhs, rhs, epsilon) (since 5.1.0)

detaileddescription.para: Constructs the floating-point detail::value<T> with the given tolerance, instead of the one derived from the number of decimals of the value.

briefdescription.para: User-defined literal operator to create a named boolean constant.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the character sequence representing the literal.
The size of the character sequence.

simplesect.para: A detail::named_bool instance, with the value true, reported by its name.

xrefdescription.para: use a plain bool and a check message (since 5.1.0)

detaileddescription.para: This user-defined literal operator creates a named boolean constant, with the value true, from a string literal (for example, "feature_enabled"_b).

The returned detail::named_bool converts implicitly to bool, and the expression formatter prints its name instead of its value. With the operators in the operators namespace, a comparison like "feature_enabled"_b == flag is true when flag is true, and, when it fails, it is reported as feature_enabled == false; the same applies to eq ("feature_enabled"_b, flag). Without these operators, the comparison is a plain bool expression, and its operands are not reported.

briefdescription.para: Deprecated literal operators and wrappers for typed operands.

detaileddescription.para: Literals such as 1_i and 42_f create strongly typed operands, whilst wrappers like mt::to_i{expression} convert dynamic values, so that the (deprecated) overloaded operators can compare and report them.

Deprecated
The literals of the literals namespace, the to_* type wrappers, to_t<T>, and the two-argument mt::approx (value, epsilon) are deprecated since 5.1.0, in favour of the function comparators mt::eq(), mt::ne(), mt::lt(), mt::le(), mt::gt(), and mt::ge(), which compare and report the plain values, and of the function comparator mt::approx (lhs, rhs, epsilon), which sets the tolerance explicitly. The compiler reports their use.
The integer literals follow the C++ syntax: decimal, hexadecimal (0x10_i), binary (0b101_i), and octal (010_i, which is 8), with digit separators (1'000_i). A decimal point, an exponent, or a value that does not fit in the type of the literal (e.g. 300_u8) is a compilation error.

The floating-point literals are written with decimal digits and a decimal point, optionally with digit separators (1'000.000'5_d), but without an exponent; they can have up to 19 digits before the decimal point and 19 after it, otherwise the compilation fails.

The floating-point literals (1.5_d) and wrappers (mt::to_d{ 1.5 }) compare with a tolerance of one unit of the last decimal written (0.1 for 1.5), so that 1.45 == 1.5_d is true. All six comparisons apply it consistently: values within the tolerance are equal, and neither less nor greater. Plain floating-point values compare exactly. The tolerance depends on the digits written, and on which operand is wrapped; to set it explicitly, use mt::approx (lhs, rhs, epsilon).
